newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs hit by renewed EMU worries.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs hit by renewed EMU worries.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds (OLOs) went south with other government bond markets on Friday as a French election poll rekindled doubts about Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) happening on time.

Dealers said investors would likely take the poll, which showed the centre-right government with only a wafer-thin lead over the opposition socialists and communists, as another reason to stay sidelined rather than sell.
The benchmark 10-year OLO yielded 6.03 percent at around 0800 GMT, down from 5.99 percent in late Thursday trade after the poll came out, but little changed from the opening.

France's socialists support EMU, but not the Maastricht Treaty deficit criterion, which they call an arbitrary target. They oppose new austerity measures France must take to hit the target and satisfy German demands for a strict interpretation of the criteria.

French bonds were little changed against German paper, but money market rates and the French franc came off, pushing the Belgian franc down to 20.6349/64 to the mark from 20.6335/45 at Thursday's close.
Three-month Belgian Treasury bill yields firmed to 3.20/25 percent from 3.18/21. One-week repos were steady.
"The poll has had some effect in the money market. We're down three or four basis points while France is down 10, but most of the damage in OLOs is at the long end," one OLO trader said.
Another trader agreed the front end of the OLO curve remained fairly steady, but he noted that flows were low.
"All these uncertainties are just another reason investors will stay sidelined," he said.
